one_month_reasoning: Window 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05. Inside it: (1) Nokia Q3 2026 report on 22 Oct 2026 (stated in the Q2 6-K [1]; StockAnalysis lists 22 Oct before market open [6]). Q3 is largely pre-announced: net sales +3% to 7% q/q and comparable operating profit largely flat on Q2's EUR 434m [1]. The swing factors are AI & Cloud order intake after Q2's EUR 2.8bn (CEO: 'order patterns in this market can be lumpy and we should not expect this level of intake every quarter' [2]), free cash flow after Q2's -EUR 732m [1] with the CFO tracking 'the low end' of 55-75% conversion [2], and whether the 'somewhat above the midpoint' FY26 guide holds [2]. An independent newsletter noted after Q2 that the stock 'follows cash flow', not headlines [36]. (2) Ericsson Q3 on 15 Oct 2026 [22] (RAN read-across). (3) Arista Q3 on 3 Nov 2026 after the close [25] (AI-networking read-across). The FWA sale to Inseego closed on 1 Oct 2026 [10] and is immaterial. Today's ~+6.5% rise came with a broad optical/networking rally (CIEN from $389.69 to ~$436 intraday [13]) and no Nokia-specific news, so I allow slight mean reversion: median ~$10.75, just under spot. Width: 62% annual realized vol / 3.5 = ~0.177; I use a two-component mix (80% sigma 0.16, 20% sigma 0.26, effective ~0.184) to fatten the tails for the earnings day. I make no directional earnings call because the Q3 P&L is pre-guided; my below-spot fair value is a 12-month argument and barely moves a 1-month forecast.

fair_value.method: 65% P/E: NTM comparable EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.380 x 17x (profit-mix-weighted multiple, at the 16.1x NTM median of 11 systems peers) = EUR 6.46 = $7.28; 35% DCF: 2028 FCF EUR 2.065bn (CMD 2028 OP midpoint 2.95bn x 70% CMD conversion) growing 5% to 2032, 9.5% discount rate (10Y 5.31% + 4.23% ERP), 3% terminal growth, plus EUR 2.776bn net cash over 5.802bn shares = EUR 6.48 = $7.30. Blend 0.65 x 7.28 + 0.35 x 7.30 = $7.29 at ECB EUR/USD 1.1269, 1 ADS = 1 share.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM comparable EPS at Oct-2027 EUR 0.380 (0.25 x FY27E 0.361 + 0.75 x FY28E 0.386) x 17x NTM P/E = EUR 6.46; x 1.1269 = $7.28 per ADS

inputs_detail.derivation: Guidance EUR 2.1-2.6bn [1]; management tracking 'somewhat above the midpoint' (2.35bn) [2]. H1 2026 actual EUR 735m [1] + Q3 largely flat on Q2's 434m [1] leaves ~EUR 1.23bn for Q4 (2.40 - 0.735 - 0.434), consistent with the CFO's 'meaningful improvement' in Q4 [2].

FY2025 recast comparable OP EUR 2,092m [1] to the 2028 CMD midpoint EUR 2.95bn [3] is ~12.2% a year; 2027 at 2.75bn is slightly above that straight line. Consensus FY2027 EPS EUR 0.408 [5] implies ~EUR 3.07bn OP ((0.408 x 5.802 / 0.735) - 0.15), above the 2028 midpoint a year early, so I do not adopt it.

Midpoint of the CMD target EUR 2.7-3.2bn by 2028 [3]. Cross-check from segment targets: NI 2025 sales EUR 7,646m [1] x 1.07^3 (6-8% CAGR [3]) x 15% (13-17% margin [3]) = EUR 1.405bn + MI ~EUR 1.6bn (judgment: 'grow from a base of EUR 1.5 billion' [3]) - common EUR 0.15bn [3] = EUR 2.855bn, so the midpoint is not conservative.
FY2026 assumption EUR 150-250m positive [1]; I assume a lower recurring level, as part of 2026 reflects non-recurring investment gains.

inputs_detail.value: FY2027E EUR 0.361, FY2028E EUR 0.386, NTM at Oct-2027 EUR 0.380

inputs_detail.derivation: Peer NTM P/E median 16.1x, range 8.0-43.4x (11 peers, comps). Mix-weighted SOTP: Optical+IP were 70.3% of FY2025 NI sales (3,019 + 2,594 of 7,986 [4]) and get 22x (Cisco 22.4x: Nokia's 10-12% Optical+IP sales CAGR target [3] is Cisco-like growth, not Ciena's +65% or Arista's +26.5% EPS growth); Fixed (29.7%) gets the fixed-access median 14.7x (CALX 16.1, ADTN 14.7, HLIT 14.3) -> NI 0.703 x 22 + 0.297 x 14.7 = 19.8x. MI gets Ericsson 13.8x. 2028E OP weights NI 1.405 / MI 1.6 = 47/53 -> 0.47 x 19.8 + 0.53 x 13.8 = 16.6x, rounded to 17x (+6% vs the 16.1x median, inside the range). Using 24x for Optical+IP still gives 17.3x.
ECB reference rate 2026-10-06 [7], held flat; F-4: each ADS represents one Nokia share [38].

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCF EUR 2.065bn 2028, 2.168 2029, 2.277 2030, 2.390 2031, 2.510 2032 (mid-year, discounted to 2027-10-06); discount rate 9.5%; terminal g 3%; EV EUR 34.79bn + net cash 2.776bn = 37.57bn / 5.802bn = EUR 6.48 = $7.30

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of the CMD target 'free cash flow conversion from comparable operating profit of between 65% and 75%' [3].
NI targets 6-8% sales CAGR [3] and is ~39% of sales (7,646 / 19,480 FY2025 recast [1]); MI's target is to grow profit from a EUR 1.5bn base [3], i.e. low growth; group ~4-5%, I use 5%.

US 10-year par yield 5.31% on 2026-10-05 [8] + beta 1.0 x Damodaran implied ERP 4.23% [9] = 9.54%. Beta 1.0 is judgment: above the 0.77 five-year beta on StockAnalysis [6] because the stock now trades with the AI-optical cohort at 62% realized volatility.
Below the NI 6-8% sales CAGR target [3]; MI is low-growth.
30 June 2026 [1]; held flat to the horizon (no verified build of H2-2026/2027 FCF less dividends and EUR 700-800m restructuring cash [1]).

bear.story: AI & Cloud intake normalises after the lumpy EUR 2.8bn Q2 [2], supply constraints [2] cap conversion, Q4 2026 misses the ~EUR 1.23bn needed and OP stalls near EUR 2.45bn in 2027-28: NTM EPS ~EUR 0.32 ((2.45 + 0.10) x 0.735 / 5.802 = 0.323) x ~14.4x (Ericsson 13.8x NTM) = EUR 4.66 = $5.25. Price is the conditional median of the lowest quartile of my ladder.

base.story: FY26 lands ~EUR 2.4bn, 2027 OP ~2.75-3.0bn, NTM EPS ~EUR 0.395 (between my 0.380 and the consensus-anchored 0.420); the AI-optical premium partly fades, with the NTM P/E going from 24.5x today (EUR 9.62 / 0.392 NTM consensus [5][7]) to ~21x (EUR 8.43 / 0.395), about 40% of the way to the 17x mix multiple. $9.50 is the ladder median.

bull.story: The optical/DCI upcycle persists (Dell'Oro: market +15% y/y and DCI +45% in 2Q26 [33]; Nokia top-3 [33]), AI & Cloud orders keep converting, and 2028 OP runs above the CMD top end (EPS ~EUR 0.44 needs ~3.37bn OP). The market re-files Nokia with optical/IP leaders (CIEN 38.1x, ANET 43.4x NTM) at ~35x: EUR 15.3 = $17.25, back to the June 2026 high area ($17.45 52-week high). Price is the conditional median of the top quartile of my ladder.

comps_summary.peer_range: NTM P/E (Oct-2026 to Sep-2027, S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, each fiscal year time-weighted onto the same window): 8.0x (AVNW) to 43.4x (ANET); median 16.1x, mean 21.1x. Cross-check on calendar 2027 EPS: median 15.1x, range 7.6-41.1x. EV/EBITDA: 7.84x (ADTN) to 60.41x (CIEN), median 25.26x, but these are TTM values from the statistics pages (no forward EBITDA consensus was available to me), so they are not used in the valuation. StockAnalysis 'Forward PE' was not used because it mixes fiscal years (e.g. ADTN shows 21.08x vs 14.7x NTM).
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM P/E, +6% vs the 16.1x peer median and well inside the range. NOK itself trades at 24.5x NTM consensus (EUR 9.62 / 0.392 = 0.25 x 0.343 + 0.75 x 0.408 [5][7]), +52% vs the median.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The small premium is only profit mix, and that mix is structural for the horizon: Optical+IP are 70.3% of NI sales [4] with CMD targets of 10-12% growth and a 13-17% NI margin [3], so about 47% of 2028E OP sits in a business whose closest growth match (Cisco) trades at 22.4x. The other 53% (MI) is Ericsson-like at 13.8x. No AI-optical premium beyond that is justified: Nokia's Optical+IP growth target is well below Ciena's (+65%) and Arista's (+26.5%) next-year EPS growth, and NI's FY2025 margin of 9.8% [4] is below the systems leaders'. Excluded peers: LITE, COHR, FN, GLW (component, contract-manufacturing and materials makers, not systems vendors); MSI (public-safety LMR/software, much less cyclical); RBBN (FY26 EPS consensus $0.06 from 4 analysts makes its P/E meaningless); ZTE (only one analyst estimate on StockAnalysis, A-shares not trading since 30 Sep); UI (one analyst).

thesis_break_reason: $5.75 = EUR 5.10 = 13.0x today's NTM consensus EPS EUR 0.392 [5], below Ericsson's 13.8x and in the bottom of the 11-peer range. At that level the market would give no value to the AI & Cloud optical/IP franchise and would expect earnings to fall short of consensus by more than 15%. That most likely means a fundamental break (AI & Cloud orders cancelled or not converting, the FY26 guide cut below EUR 2.1bn, or the 2028 EUR 2.7-3.2bn target abandoned), not ordinary volatility. My ladder gives ~17% odds of closing below it.

key_uncertainties: Durability and conversion of AI & Cloud orders: EUR 2.8bn in Q2, about half to convert within 12 months, management warns intake is lumpy [2].
Q4 2026 execution: ~EUR 1.23bn comparable OP needed for ~EUR 2.4bn [1][2]; an independent newsletter flagged that one delayed contract would push the year toward the low end [36].
Estimate gap: FY2027 consensus EPS EUR 0.408 [5] implies ~EUR 3.07bn OP vs my 2.75bn; if consensus is right, the P/E leg rises from $7.28 to ~$8.05.
Multiple: whether the market keeps paying 24.5x NTM (AI-optical cohort) vs 16.1x for systems peers; NOK moved with Ciena today.
Cash: Q2 FCF -EUR 732m, H1 -EUR 104m [1], FY26 conversion at the low end of 55-75% [2], EUR 700-800m restructuring cash in 2026 [1].

Defense is not separately disclosed: 'Mission Critical Enterprise & Defense' customer sales were EUR 448m in Q2 and EUR 914m in H1 2026 [1] (an upper bound that includes non-defense customers); Nokia Defense incubation unit launched at the CMD [3]; Nokia Federal Solutions/Lockheed Martin 5G.MIL solution, no contract value [37]. Not in the valuation.
EUR/USD: valuation is in EUR; a 5% EUR move changes the ADS value ~5% [7].
reasoning: Facts (re-verified at source this round): Q2 2026 net sales EUR 4,815m, comparable OP EUR 434m (NI 166m, MI 310m, common -42m), comparable diluted EPS EUR 0.07, FCF -EUR 732m, net cash EUR 2,776m, 5,801.9m diluted shares, AI & Cloud sales EUR 446m (+105% cc) and orders EUR 2.8bn; Optical +20%, IP +16%, Fixed -2% [1]. The FY26 guide is EUR 2.1-2.6bn (a 0.1bn technical revision from discontinued operations) [1]; the CMD targets 2028 OP EUR 2.7-3.2bn with 65-75% FCF conversion [3]. Supervisor findings I accepted after checking the primary pages: (a) the 5.06% I used as the 10-year yield was the 5-year; the 10-year was 5.31% [8]; (b) the CMD conversion target is 65-75%, not 55-85% [3]; (c) my 25.95x peer median mixed fiscal bases and included component makers. I rebuilt the peer set as 11 systems/network-equipment vendors on one NTM basis (S&P Global consensus via StockAnalysis, each fiscal year time-weighted onto Oct-2026 to Sep-2027): median 16.1x (calendar-2027 cross-check 15.1x, matching the supervisor's 7-peer figure). Where I differ from the supervisor: I keep my bottom-up NTM EPS EUR 0.380 rather than 0.421, because the CMD segment targets build to ~EUR 2.86bn 2028 OP, not the 3.2bn top end. I also value NI at ~20x (Cisco-like Optical+IP at 22x, Fixed at 14.7x, weighted by verified FY2025 unit sales [4]) rather than 26x, so my group multiple is 17x, not 20x. The P/E leg is $7.28, the DCF $7.30 (9.5% = 5.31% + 4.23% ERP [9]) and the blended FV $7.29, 33% below spot. Distribution: the stock trades at 24.5x NTM with an AI-optical premium that has lasted all year, and valuation gaps close slowly, so I put ~25% weight on the FV gap and ~75% on a drift-neutral lognormal (mean log return -sigma^2/2 at sigma ~0.54): median ~exp(0.75 x -0.066 + 0.25 x ln(7.29/10.84)) x 10.84 = ~$9.35, rounded up to $9.50 for the industry evidence (Dell'Oro 2Q26 optical +15%, DCI +45%, Nokia top-3 [33]; Cignal AI 'Nokia Optical up 29%' in 1Q26 [35]). Ladder = 85% lognormal sigma 0.48 + 15% sigma 0.80 (effective ~0.54, a bit under the 62% realized because part of it was the June spike), median $9.50, mean ~$11.0. Scenario prices are the conditional medians of the bottom quartile, the middle half and the top quartile ($5.25 / $9.50 / $17.25 at 25/50/25%), so they match the ladder. Analyst average target $14.97 (14 analysts) [5] is evidence only. Alternative-lane sources (Dell'Oro, Cignal AI, an independent newsletter) are context and do not move the multiple. The 22 peer data pages keep my in-lane share low (4 of 38). Social posts (StockTwits sentiment, an unverified $21 target) are excluded. No option data was used.
